#: This is an example Panboticon configuration file. Store your version of this JSON file in ~/.panboticon.json. If you wish for this file to be elsewhere, set PANBOTICON_CONFIG in your environment to its pathname or provide the -c option every time you invoke the panboticon command. Any of these may be set in the environment and that will take precedence over this configuration file. Some subcommands allow some of these to be overridden by flags. These take precedence over both environment variables and this configuration file.

AWS region name (e.g. "us-west-2"). If this is specified and PANBOTICON_AZ is not, a random availability zone within the region will be chosen when needed. If this is not specified and PANBOTICON_AZ is, this is inferred from PANBOTICON_AZ.

AWS availability zone name (e.g. "us-west-2b") or ID (e.g. "usw1-az3"). If this is specified and PANBOTICON_REGION is also specified, they must agree. If this is specified and PANBOTICON_REGION is not, PANBOTICON_REGION is inferred from this.
AWS VPC ID where Panboticon instances are launched.

AWS subnet ID where Panboticon instances are launched. If this is specified, it must be in PANBOTICON_VPC_ID. If this is not specified, a suitable subnet in PANBOTICON_VPC_ID and PANBOTICON_AZ is chosen.

AWS IAM instance profile for Panboticon instances. This is how you'll give your Panboticon instance access to use AWS APIs. The instance profile's role must attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy.
AWD EC2 instance type for Panboticon instances.
Usernames for the human and bot users.
Email addresses for the human user, which will be configured in ~/.gitconfig as the author of commits.

GitHub App details for the bot user. The App ID can be found on <https://github.com/settings/apps/PANBOTICON_BOT_USER>. App Installation IDs can be found in the last component of the URL like <https://github.com/apps/PANBOTICON_BOT_USER/installations/INSTALLATION_ID> or <https://github.com/organizations/ORGANIZATION/settings/installations/INSTALLATION_ID> linked by Organization from <https://github.com/settings/apps/PANBOTICON_BOT_USER/installations>. The private key can be generated during app setup and given as a pathname (relative or absolute, understands ~) or a 1Password `op://` URL.
Login shells to assign to the human and bot users.
TERM environment variable to assign when SSH'ing to Panboticon instances.
CIDR prefixes that should reject the bot user's connections (via iptables).

Path to a program containing additional bootstrapping commands to be executed locally (i.e. where Panboticon itself is running). The program will be given the name of a single Panboticon instance as its only argument. Use this to e.g. `panboticon scp` files to all your Panboticon instances.
Paths to shell programs containing additional bootstrapping commands for human and bot users. These will be executed interactively while launching instances to facilitate e.g. OAuth flows.

Slack incoming webhook URL humans and bots alike can use to send messages to Slack. See <https://docs.slack.dev/messaging/sending-messages-using-incoming-webhooks/>. Will be made available in the environment of PANBOTICON_LOCAL_BOOTSTRAP, PANBOTICON_HUMAN_BOOTSTRAP and PANBOTICON_BOT_BOOTSTRAP so you can stash it wherever you like.
This comment allows all the lines above to have trailing commas.
